messages.text:
I need you to do a deep dive on 2D/2.5D (faked 3D) procedural graphics rendering in C#. All of the absolute bleeding edge tech and insights and tricks as of now (Feb 2026). Layering, blending, parallax, pre and post processing, etc., every graphics term/buzzword you can think of across the board in order to build out a new graphics rendering engine for my game so that we have something that doesn't LOOK "indie" or MS Paint or like one dude with no graphical skills made it. 

Building complex forms from basic shapes and then baking those forms for animation, multiple layers of detail, not pixel art, SVG. 

The game itself is a cross-genre (every genre) multiversal dungeon crawler so the aesthetic should be cohesive yet varied

Format the resulting Game Design Document for the AI agent in Visual Studio Code to follow.

This is a meaty request — I want to make sure the research and resulting GDD hit the mark. A couple quick clarifications:

These answers will shape whether the research focuses on shader pipelines, GPU-accelerated vector rendering, specific framework APIs, and what performance constraints to design around. Once you pick, I'll kick off the deep research immediately.

Q: What's your C# rendering foundation / framework?
A: Current is Silk.NET with OpenGL 3.3 Core profile. The window system, input, and GL bindings all come from Silk.NET 2.21.0

Q: Target platforms?
A: PC (Windows/Mac/Linux)

Q: For the SVG-based procedural shapes — what level of runtime generation are you envisioning?
A: Not sure yet — recommend best approach
Got it — Silk.NET 2.21.0 with OpenGL 3.3 Core, PC-only, and you want a best-approach recommendation on the generation pipeline. That's plenty to work with. Let me dive deep on this.

Q: What's your C# rendering foundation / framework?
A: Current is Silk.NET with OpenGL 3.3 Core profile. The window system, input, and GL bindings all come from Silk.NET 2.21.0, BUT I am open to switching to something else.

Q: Target platforms?
A: PC (Windows/Mac/Linux)

Q: For the SVG-based procedural shapes — what level of runtime generation are you envisioning?
A: Not sure yet — recommend best approach

You know what, so you know what we are dealing with, I've included the master plan document.

We are on the cusp of a complete graphics overhaul and I want the NEW system to be astounding.

[1 private attachment omitted]

Let me read through your master plan first so the research is properly grounded in your actual architecture and vision.

Excellent — this is an incredibly ambitious project. I now have the full picture: The Infinite Labyrinth's procedural graphics stack (SDFs, WFC, compute shaders, L-Systems, sprite stacking), the Arch ECS + SpacetimeDB architecture, and the fact that the master plan currently references Raylib-cs but you're open to switching (you mentioned Silk.NET with OpenGL 3.3 Core in conversation). 

The scope is clear enough that I can dive straight into deep research. Let me get this going.

Your procedural 2D/2.5D rendering engine technical design document is ready. It covers the complete architecture for a C#/Silk.NET/OpenGL 3.3 engine featuring a hybrid compose-bake-animate pipeline using SDF/MSDF shaders, SkiaSharp vector composition, normal-mapped 2D lighting with shadow casting, multi-pass post-processing (bloom, volumetric light shafts, color grading), and a universe style system that drives all visuals from a single parameterized data structure. The document includes the full module dependency graph, GLSL shader implementations, sprite batching architecture, procedural content generation systems (WFC dungeons, character/item composition, noise-based textures), an eight-phase incremental build plan, project structure, and OpenGL 3.3 Core compatibility verification for every technique.

Good, this covers the rendering, now I want you to do another round of research to improve the visual style of the game, the aesthetic. All of that was essentially the tools and the canvas and the paints, now I want you to create the plan for how the artist uses them so to speak. What I mean is, the game looks very IVAN/CoQ, low fidelity/style, it looks boring and bland, how do we use the tools to make a visually pleasing, vibrant, and uniquely STYLIZED product?

Also here is the agents.md we are working with in VS Code for additional context.

[1 private attachment omitted]

Let me read through the AGENTS.md first to understand the constraints the AI agent is working under, then I'll kick off the research.

This is crystal clear — Phase N built the rendering infrastructure but the game still *looks* like a roguelike that a programmer made. You want the art direction document: the visual style bible that tells the engine *what* to paint, not *how* to paint. Let me dive in.

The research is still running — those deep dives typically take 2–5 minutes to come back with results. It's working through all 14 sections of the visual style bible request right now (case studies from Hollow Knight/Hades/Dead Cells, shape language theory, color theory, VFX "juice" techniques, etc.).

Once it returns, I'll format the full Visual Style Bible as a document and deliver it to you. Hang tight!

It's been an hour and a half
